chapters.summary: After Daniel and his friends are carried into exile in Babylon, they hold fast to their faith, refusing the king's food, and God blesses them with unmatched wisdom.
keyPoints: Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food and wine, asking instead for only vegetables and water.
God grants Daniel favor before the chief eunuch; after ten days of testing, he and his friends look healthier and better nourished than those who ate the king's food.
God gives Daniel and his three friends knowledge and skill in every branch of learning, and Daniel is especially gifted in understanding visions and dreams.
chapters.application: Let us hold fast to our faith without compromise even in a pagan environment, trusting that God will watch over us. Today, may we honor the Lord as supreme in every area of life, trusting in his provision and guidance.

chapters.summary: Daniel interprets King Nebuchadnezzar's dream, revealing God's supreme sovereignty over history and his eternal kingdom.
keyPoints: The king demands that his wise men tell him his dream and interpret it; when none can, he grows furious and orders the wise men put to death.
Daniel asks God to reveal the mystery; once he receives the revelation, he blesses God and boldly interprets the dream before the king.
In the dream a great statue is shattered by a stone cut without hands, symbolizing how the kingdoms of this world will finally give way to the kingdom of God.
chapters.application: When we face the unknown and difficult challenges, let us, like Daniel, seek God first, trusting that he governs all things, and boldly bear witness to his wisdom and power.

chapters.summary: Daniel's three friends are thrown into a fiery furnace for refusing to worship the golden image, and God wondrously preserves them unharmed, displaying his power and faithfulness.
keyPoints: King Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and commands the people of every nation to worship it when the music sounds, threatening to cast into a fiery furnace anyone who refuses.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image, standing firm in their trust in God even when threatened with death.
God is present with them in the furnace and delivers them from the flames; the king and all the people see his glory, and the king praises God.
chapters.application: When our faith is put to the test, let us, like Daniel's friends, stand firm regardless of circumstances, trusting that God governs all things - he will be with us and give us strength to face any hardship.

chapters.summary: For his prideful boasting, King Nebuchadnezzar is punished by God with the loss of his reason, living like a beast, until he humbly acknowledges the authority of the Most High and is restored - a testimony to God's rule.
keyPoints: The king dreams of a great tree cut down, though its stump remains in the ground - a vision foretelling that his pride will be punished.
Daniel interprets the dream and urges the king to practice righteousness to avert disaster, but the king does not heed the warning, and a year later boasts of his own achievements.
God causes the king to lose his sanity, and he eats grass like cattle, until he lifts his eyes to heaven and humbly gives glory to God - only then is he restored.
chapters.application: Let us always keep a humble heart, acknowledging that everything is by God's grace, and never boast in our own achievements. When pride rises within us, let us remember that God governs all things and turn back in time - he will surely show mercy.

chapters.summary: King Belshazzar defiles the vessels from the temple at his banquet, sees handwriting appear on the wall, and Daniel interprets it, foretelling the fall of Babylon.
keyPoints: King Belshazzar drinks from the temple vessels and praises idols, profaning God.
Mysterious writing appears on the wall that no one can interpret, and Daniel is summoned to explain it.
Daniel declares God's judgment, and that very night Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's sovereignty over all things, avoid pride and arrogance, and live with humility and reverence, for God will surely judge every act of profanity and rebellion.

chapters.summary: Daniel is thrown into the lions' den through a plot against him for his faithful service to God, and God preserves him unharmed, displaying his faithfulness and power.
keyPoints: Daniel is appointed chief administrator for his outstanding ability, arousing the jealousy of his colleagues.
His colleagues use the king's decree to trap Daniel, but he continues to pray to God as always.
God shuts the lions' mouths, and Daniel is kept safe, while his accusers are instead devoured by the lions.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us keep praying to God every day, trusting in his protection. God watches over the faithful and grants peace even in the midst of trouble.

chapters.summary: In a vision Daniel sees four beasts representing four empires; in the end the Son of man receives the kingdom, and the saints possess the kingdom forever, serving God.
keyPoints: Daniel sees four beasts rise out of the sea, symbolizing Babylon, the Medes and Persians, Greece, and Rome.
One like the Son of man comes with the clouds and is given authority, glory, and a kingdom, that all peoples should serve him forever.
The saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess it forever; Daniel is troubled in spirit yet keeps the matter to himself.
chapters.application: However the world may change, God remains in control of all things. Let us look with faith to his eternal kingdom, holding fast to hope amid turmoil, and live faithfully.

chapters.summary: In a vision Daniel sees a ram and a male goat locked in battle, and a small horn's arrogance; the angel Gabriel explains that this concerns the judgment and kingdom of the last days.
keyPoints: Daniel sees a vision of a ram and a male goat, and the goat defeats the ram.
Four horns grow up on the goat's head, and out of one of them comes a small horn that attacks the saints and the daily sacrifice.
The angel Gabriel interprets the vision, foretelling Persia, Greece, the kings who arise after Greece is divided, and the judgment of the last days.
chapters.application: Amid the chaos of the world, let us hold fast to the belief that God governs history; let us humbly rely on him and wait for his righteous kingdom to come.

chapters.summary: Daniel fasts and prays for his people, pleading for God to forgive Israel's sin, and receives from the angel Gabriel the revelation of the seventy weeks.
keyPoints: Learning from the scriptures that Jerusalem would lie desolate for seventy years, Daniel fasts, puts on sackcloth and ashes, and prays earnestly.
He confesses Israel's sin, pleads for God's forgiveness, and asks God to restore the temple and the holy city.
Gabriel comes and reveals the prophecy of the seventy weeks, concerning the Messiah and the outcome of the last days.
chapters.application: Let us follow Daniel's example, praying earnestly in times of hardship, confessing our own faults, trusting that God hears us, and waiting for his promises to be fulfilled.

chapters.summary: By the river Hiddekel (Tigris), Daniel sees a vision, and an angel reveals to him things to come, encouraging him to be strong and courageous.
keyPoints: Daniel mourns and fasts for three weeks on behalf of the people of Israel, and then sees a vision.
A glorious angel, clothed in linen, is sent to explain the vision to Daniel.
The angel encourages Daniel not to be afraid, but to be strong and take courage.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, let us follow Daniel's example, praying earnestly, trusting that God will hear us and grant us strength and peace, so that we may be strong and courageous in facing every challenge.

chapters.summary: Daniel 11, through the angel's prophecy, reveals the wars between the kings of Persia and Greece and the kings of the South and North, culminating in the end-time Antichrist's arrogance and downfall.
keyPoints: The angel reveals to Daniel the future course of history, including the rise and fall of the kings of Persia and Greece.
The king of the South and the king of the North wage repeated wars, marked by marriage alliances and betrayals, showing the instability of human power.
In the last days a king will exalt and magnify himself, attacking the saints, but will finally be destroyed, pointing to God's sovereignty.
chapters.application: Facing the world's conflicts, let us trust that God governs history, hold fast to faith amid the turmoil, and wait for his final victory.

chapters.summary: Daniel 12 describes the great tribulation of the last days, the resurrection and reward of the righteous, and Daniel receiving revelation about the time of the end and being blessed.
keyPoints: Michael shall stand up, and a time of great trouble will come, but everyone whose name is found written in the book will be delivered.
Those who sleep in the dust will awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, and the wise will shine like the stars.
Daniel receives revelation concerning a time, times, and half a time, and is told to wait until the end.
chapters.application: Facing an uncertain future, let us hold fast to faith and remain faithful to the end, for God governs history and his promises will surely be fulfilled.
